## git merge vs git rebase

**Merge** — joins two branches, creates merge commit. History shows exactly what happened.

```
main:    A---B---C---M
                    /
feat:        D---E
```

**Rebase** — replays commits on top of target. History looks linear, but rewrites commit SHAs.

```
main:    A---B---C
feat:            D'--E'   (new SHAs, same changes)
```

---

## When to use

**Use merge when:**
- Merging feature → main (preserves true history)
- Working on shared/public branch (safe, no SHA rewrite)
- Want audit trail of when branches joined

**Use rebase when:**
- Updating local feature branch with upstream main changes
- Cleaning up messy WIP commits before PR review
- Want linear history for `git log` readability

---

## Tradeoffs

| | Merge | Rebase |
|---|---|---|
| History | Honest, non-linear | Clean, linear |
| Safety | Safe on shared branches | **Dangerous on shared branches** |
| Conflict resolution | Once, at merge | Once per replayed commit |
| Bisect/blame | Harder with many merges | Easier |

---

## Golden rule

**Never rebase public/shared branches.** Rewriting SHAs breaks everyone else's history. Only rebase commits that exist only on your local machine.

Common workflow: `rebase main onto feature` locally → `merge feature into main` via PR.
